# Certify-the-Checker

> A "no issues found" (CLEAN) result from a code checker is only true for what was actually checked: the build settings and
> the kinds of input that were run. Six small C examples compare three free checkers (clang --analyze, gcc -fanalyzer,
> cppcheck) with running the code under AddressSanitizer/UBSan, and measure test coverage depth with gcov. A short standard
> describes how to report a CLEAN result with its scope.

Scope: six hand-written teaching examples, not a survey of real projects; results depend on tool versions (Ubuntu 24.04,
gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3, cppcheck 2.13.0). Not a vulnerability report.

- [README.md](README.md): results table, how results are decided, quick start
- [STANDARD-v0.md](STANDARD-v0.md): the reporting standard (plain-language version first)
- [examples/expected-results.txt](examples/expected-results.txt): results in machine-readable form
- [schema/readout.schema.json](schema/readout.schema.json): format of each readout
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): what changed in each version
- [DIGEST.md](DIGEST.md): every text file of this repo in one document
